Ava — thanks for the appendix and the clear asks. We reviewed the evidence section and can commit to an initial onboarding package plus an audit-ready manifest for the pilot. High-level commitments and clarifications below; I'll follow up with an agenda for the workshop.

1) Evidence bundle contents (what we'll deliver)
- One-time onboarding package: sample telemetry export (JSONL + Parquet), synthetic probe logs for the pilot region for the previous 7 days, per-route token-level cost & latency CSV, and a signed evidence manifest (see attached rwi_evidence_manifest_template.xlsx).
- Ongoing exports: aggregated SLO snapshots (daily), raw sampling subset (1% sampled request traces, up to 100K traces/month), and probe results (1-min cadence synthetic probes).

2) Measurement semantics (our defaults and rationale)
- Availability: measured at the API gateway egress (response codes 2xx considered success). 1-second resolution timestamps, aggregated into 1-minute windows for rolling availability.
- Latency: we will report both p95 and p99 for end-to-end request latency measured at response egress. For model-internal generation time we provide pod metrics separately (useful for root cause but not for customer SLA calc).
- Burst/partial degradations: we support configurable "burst windows" up to 10s for transient spikes; persistent degradations are computed over standard 5-minute windows.

3) Retention & access
- Raw trace TTL: 12 months (we can extend to 24 months under an enterprise addendum).
- Export model: S3 presigned export or shared Drive link; access control via your SSO and our audit logs.
- Crypto: evidence manifests are signed and references to KMS key IDs will be included when requested.

4) Disputes and credits workflow
- First step: evidence submission (we provide zipped manifest + sample traces).
- Reconciliation window: 10 business days for joint analysis; if unresolved, escalate to our Reliability Council for final determination.
- Service credits: formula-based; we will include worked examples for typical scenarios in the workshop.

Next steps: can you share the list of endpoints/routes you want included in the pilot, and pick two 1-hour slots for the workshop (our suggested engineer attendees: karthik, rishi, lauren).

I'll attach the evidence manifest template in my next email and include sample CSVs exported from a staging tenant so you can see the column formats.

Quick technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- Latency definition: we measure request latency at our API gateway egress (time between request received timestamp and final bytes sent). For multi-turn/chat flows we provide per-turn p95/p99 and an aggregated session view; please indicate which you prefer for the SLA.
- Sampling approach: 1% sampled request traces gives a statistically useful set for root cause while keeping export sizes manageable. We can make sampling deterministic (hash-based) to ensure repeatability across exports.
- Synthetic probes: 1-minute cadence across three probe types: small prompt (warm cache), cold-start prompt (empty KV cache), and long-context prompt to exercise sequence-length behavior. This helps distinguish KV-cache warmup vs model saturation.
- Regional weighting: if Novacorp wants multi-region weighting (e.g., 70% us-west, 30% eu), we will apply a weighted aggregation for availability and latency; we need the region mapping for each route.

I'll prepare a short appendix describing the probe types and a sample export schema. Also note: model quantization variants can change tail latency; if you expect to use quantized variants in production, we should lock the model profile for SLA measurement.

-Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ava — appreciate the prompt. A few contractual things to confirm so we can prepare draft SOW language for procurement:

- Credit calculation: we'll provide the explicit formula in writing (availability-based days-of-service credits and latency-tier credits tied to p99 breaches). For legal clarity we'll include worked examples for single-region and multi-region scenarios.
- Force majeure / scheduled maintenance: scheduled maintenance windows will be excluded from uptime calculations if communicated 72 hours in advance and not exceeding the contract's maintenance SLA.
- Measurement authority: Redwood's exported evidence will be the primary input; Novacorp may submit supplemental telemetry. Joint reconciliation will be the governance path.
- For the pilot: we'll provide a 30-day evidence escrow (read-only access) to the exported traces. Access provisioning typically takes 48 hours after statement of work (SOW) signature.

We will attach a lightly redlined SOW appendix for your procurement team after the workshop, and include the credit formulas and timelines. If Novacorp requires an independent third-party audit, please indicate and we can add audit support language.

Thanks — Lauren Bishop, Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
